subproblems.title: Lipschitz cut-off adapted to a compact set (step 2 of the parent proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact and ε > 0. Then there are ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ and L ∈ [0, ∞) such that ψ is L-Lipschitz, 0 ≤ ψ(x) ≤ 1 for all x, ψ = 1 on K, the set W₀ := {x : ψ(x) > 0} is contained in thickening(ε, K) = {x : dist(x, K) < ε} (Mathlib Metric.thickening ε K), and closure(W₀) is compact and contained in U (contract CompactlyContained W₀ U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → 0 < ε → ∃ (ψ : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzWith L ψ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ψ x ∧ ψ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, ψ x = 1) ∧ {x | 0 < ψ x} ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ CompactlyContained {x | 0 < ψ x} U
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (cut-off; Simon 7.2.4, chapter-07.txt lines 176–186: “choose a smooth φ : U → [0, 1] such that φ ≡ 1 in some neighborhood of K, and spt φ ⊆ {x ∈ U : dist(x, K) < ε}”). After step 2 the parent uses only that ψ is Lipschitz (constant L), 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on K, and the support properties of W₀; smoothness of ψ is never used (the smooth cut-off χ of step 4(a) is a different function, see child mass_localization). Detail: instead of mollifying an indicator function we take an explicit Lipschitz ψ with the same properties.

Notation: dist(x, K) = inf_{y∈K} |x − y| (Mathlib Metric.infDist); T_r := {x : dist(x, K) < r} and C_r := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ r} are the open and closed r-thickenings of K.

1. Case K = ∅. Take ψ ≡ 0 and L = 0. Then ψ is 0-Lipschitz, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, the condition on K is vacuous, and W₀ = {x : 0 > 0} = ∅; ∅ is contained in thickening(ε, K), and closure(∅) = ∅ is compact and contained in U.
2. Case K ≠ ∅. Since K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, there is δ > 0 with C_δ ⊆ U (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put r := min(δ, ε) > 0, ψ(x) := max(0, 1 − dist(x, K)/r) and L := 1/r.
3. Lipschitz bound. x ↦ dist(x, K) is 1-Lipschitz (Metric.lipschitz_infDist_pt). Hence |(1 − dist(x, K)/r) − (1 − dist(y, K)/r)| = |dist(x, K) − dist(y, K)|/r ≤ |x − y|/r, so x ↦ 1 − dist(x, K)/r is (1/r)-Lipschitz. Taking the maximum with the constant 0 does not increase Lipschitz constants (|max(0, s) − max(0, s′)| ≤ |s − s′|; LipschitzWith.const_max). So ψ is L-Lipschitz.
4. Bounds. ψ ≥ 0 as a maximum with 0. Since dist(x, K) ≥ 0 and r > 0, 1 − dist(x, K)/r ≤ 1, so ψ ≤ max(0, 1) = 1.
5. ψ = 1 on K: for x ∈ K, dist(x, K) = 0 (Metric.infDist_zero_of_mem), so ψ(x) = max(0, 1) = 1.
6. The positivity set. ψ(x) > 0 iff 1 − dist(x, K)/r > 0 iff dist(x, K) < r iff x ∈ T_r (Metric.mem_thickening_iff_infDist_lt, which uses K ≠ ∅). Thus W₀ = T_r.
7. W₀ = T_r ⊆ T_ε = thickening(ε, K), because r ≤ ε and open thickenings increase with the radius (Metric.thickening_mono).
8. closure(W₀) = closure(T_r) ⊆ C_r ⊆ C_δ ⊆ U (Metric.closure_thickening_subset_cthickening, Metric.cthickening_mono with r ≤ δ, and step 2). C_r is compact, being the closed thickening of a compact set in the proper space ℝ^P (IsCompact.cthickening), so its closed subset closure(W₀) is compact. Hence closure(W₀) is compact and contained in U. ∎

Remark (how the parent uses the child; not part of the proof). For α ∈ (0, 1) the set W := {ψ > α} is open (ψ is continuous), K ⊆ W ⊆ W₀ ⊆ thickening(ε, K), and closure(W) ⊆ closure(W₀) is compact and contained in U; the closed sets {ψ ≥ α} and {ψ = α} lie in W₀ ⊆ closure(W₀), hence are compact subsets of U, and {ψ = α} ∩ K = ∅. The parent slices by f := −ψ, which is again L-Lipschitz.

subproblems.title: Local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M and of the weight of an integer multiplicity representation
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (an IMRep U n). That is: M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M; and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n = μHE[n]. Let μ_R = R.measure = θ·(H^n⌞M), i.e. (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ and μ_R(K) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.imrep_local_finiteness-a1, status accepted, candidate 702e7082a5a7012f7a8f6efd9d272697e426f50b), reused with its identical frozen type. The parent proof needs it in (F1) (“μ_A ... finite on compact subsets of U”) and in steps 4, 5 and 8: it gives the local-finiteness hypotheses of the slicing sibling for μ_{R_j} and μ_{∂R_j}, the finiteness hypotheses of child good_slice_level for μ_{R_j} and μ_{T_j} on {0 < ψ < 1} ⊆ closure(W₀), and the finiteness hypothesis of child compact_outer_bound. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: step 1 (Local finiteness) of the parent proof. This is the standing hypothesis of Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733-747): the multiplicity θ is a locally H^n-integrable positive integer-valued function. In the frozen contract it is encoded by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult.

Notation: H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P (Euclid P); M = R.carrier; θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ ⊆ [0, ∞]; μ_R = R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U.

1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel (IsCompact.measurableSet).

2. (Weight of K.) Since K is measurable:
- μ_R(K) = ∫_K θ d(H^n⌞M) by the definition of withDensity (withDensity_apply);
- (H^n⌞M)⌞K = H^n⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict).
Hence μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n, after commuting the intersection.

3. The IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n ≠ ∞. By step 2, μ_R(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.

4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K, the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ. Hence 1 ≤ R.mult x, and after casting to [0, ∞], 1 ≤ θ(x).

5. (Measurability.) θ is measurable. It is the composition of the measurable map R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (field measurable_mult) with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).

6. (Unweighted measure.) H^n(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dH^n (setLIntegral_one). This is at most ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n by monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono), using the pointwise bound of step 4 on M ∩ K and the measurability of step 5. Hence M_G(P_{j,s}) ≤ M_{W₀}(P_{j,s}) for every open G”), stated for an arbitrary current X, compact set C (= {ψ = s}) and open set V (= W₀); the argument works for every G.

Notation: |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a k-covector (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm); ω is admissible for M_G if ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; M_G(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over admissible ω.

1. Case C = ∅. Every test form has support disjoint from ∅, so X(ω) = 0 for all ω; every term of the supremum defining M_G(X) is ofReal(0) = 0, so M_G(X) = 0 ≤ M_V(X).
2. Assume C ≠ ∅. Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, C) ≤ δ} ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and let V′ := {x : dist(x, C) < δ/2}. V′ is open, C ⊆ V′, and closure(V′) ⊆ {x : dist(x, C) ≤ δ/2}, a compact set (closed thickening of a compact set) contained in V.
3. A smooth cut-off. Take g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with values in [0, 1] and {g ≠ 0} = V′ (Mathlib IsOpen.exists_contDiff_support_eq). g is continuous and positive on the nonempty compact set C ⊆ V′, so a := min_C g > 0 (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Let τ := Real.smoothTransition (smooth, 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1, τ = 0 on (−∞, 0], τ = 1 on [1, ∞)) and χ(x) := τ(2g(x)/a). Then χ is smooth and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1. On the open set N := {g > a/2} ⊇ C we have 2g/a > 1, so χ = 1 on N. Where g = 0 we have χ = τ(0) = 0, so {χ ≠ 0} ⊆ V′; hence tsupport χ ⊆ closure(V′) ⊆ V and χ has compact support.
4. Scaling of the norm. For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, |cα| = |c|·|α|: the coefficients of cα on the increasing coordinate tuples are c times those of α, so the sum of their squares is c² times that of α, and √(c²s) = |c|√s.
5. Let ω be admissible for M_G and put ω₁ := χω, ω₂ := ω − ω₁ = (1 − χ)ω. ω₁ is smooth (product of smooth maps) and tsupport ω₁ ⊆ tsupport ω ∩ tsupport χ; hence ω₁ has compact support contained in U, i.e. ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and tsupport ω₁ ⊆ V. By linearity X(ω) = X(ω₁) + X(ω₂) = X(ω₁), hence ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_V(X).
7. Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_G(X) ≤ M_V(X). ∎

subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let (ν_j)_{j∈ℕ} and (κ_j)_{j∈ℕ} be measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel measurable, a < b real and A := {x : a < f(x) < b}. Assume ν_j(A) < ∞ for every j, ν_j(A) → 0 as j → ∞, and κ_j(A) < ∞ for every j. Then there are t ∈ (a, b) and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that (i) κ_j({f = t}) = 0 for every j; (ii) D_j(t) < ∞ for every j; (iii) D_{φ(j)}(t) → 0 as j → ∞; where D_j(t) := liminf_{h → 0, h > 0} ofReal(h⁻¹)·ν_j({x : t − h < f(x) < t}) ∈ [0, ∞] (liminf along the filter 𝓝[>] 0).

We can also of course choose α to be such that (5) ...”). The parent applies this lemma with ν_j := μ_{R_j}, κ_j := μ_{T_j}, f := −ψ and (a, b) := (−1, 0), so that A = {0 < ψ < 1}, {t − h < f < t} = {α < ψ < α + h} and {f = t} = {ψ = α} for α := −t ∈ (0, 1); the slicing sibling bounds M_{W₀}(P_{j,α}) by L·D_j(t).
Detail (departure in the choice of the majorant). The parent majorizes the difference quotients by −L H_j′ with H_j(s) = μ_{R_j}(W₀ ∩ {s < ψ < 1}) and bounds ∫ −H_j′ by Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc; that lemma is not in the import closure of the frozen contract. We use instead the sequential lower difference quotient G_j below, whose integral bound follows from Tonelli's theorem; the remainder of the argument (Fatou's lemma, countably many atoms, choice of the level and of the subsequence) is the parent's.

All quantities lie in [0, ∞] (0·∞ = 0); λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and “a.e.” refers to λ.

1. Measurability. Since f is Borel, A, the level sets {f = s} and the sets {t − h < f < t} are Borel.
2. Pushforward. Let ρ_j be the image of ν_j⌞A under f: ρ_j(B) = ν_j(f⁻¹(B) ∩ A) for Borel B ⊆ ℝ. Then ρ_j(ℝ) = ν_j(A) < ∞, so ρ_j is a finite Borel measure on ℝ.
3. Tonelli. For c ∈ ℝ let S_c := {(s, y) ∈ ℝ² : s − c < y < s}, a Borel set. Its sections are {y : (s, y) ∈ S_c} = (s − c, s) and {s : (s, y) ∈ S_c} = (y, y + c). Hence s ↦ ρ_j((s − c, s)) is Borel (measurability of sections of a product set, Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left), and computing (λ × ρ_j)(S_c) in both orders (Measure.prod_apply, Measure.prod_apply_symm) gives ∫ ρ_j((s − c, s)) dλ(s) = ∫ λ((y, y + c)) dρ_j(y) = ofReal(c)·ρ_j(ℝ) = ofReal(c)·ν_j(A).
4. Majorants. For k ∈ ℕ let h_k := 1/(k + 1) and F_{j,k}(s) := (k + 1)·ρ_j((s − h_k, s)). By step 3, F_{j,k} is Borel and ∫ F_{j,k} dλ = (k + 1)·ofReal(h_k)·ν_j(A) = ν_j(A). Let G_j(s) := liminf_{k→∞} F_{j,k}(s), a Borel function. Fatou's lemma gives ∫ G_j dλ ≤ liminf_k ∫ F_{j,k} dλ = ν_j(A) < ∞; hence G_j < ∞ a.e., and, intersecting countably many full-measure sets, a.e. s satisfies G_j(s) < ∞ for every j.
5. Fatou in j. H(s) := liminf_{j→∞} G_j(s) is Borel and ∫ H dλ ≤ liminf_j ∫ G_j dλ ≤ liminf_j ν_j(A) = 0, because ν_j(A) → 0. Hence H = 0 a.e.
6. Atoms. For each j the measure κ_j⌞A is finite. The level sets {f = s}, s ∈ ℝ, are pairwise disjoint, so (κ_j⌞A)({f = s}) > 0 for at most countably many s (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos). Countable sets are λ-null, so for a.e. s: (κ_j⌞A)({f = s}) = 0 for every j.
7. The level. λ((a, b)) = b − a > 0. By steps 4–6, a.e. s ∈ (a, b) satisfies H(s) = 0, G_j(s) < ∞ for every j, and (κ_j⌞A)({f = s}) = 0 for every j. A full-measure subset of a set of positive measure is nonempty, so there is t ∈ (a, b) with these three properties.
8. (i). Since t ∈ (a, b), {f = t} ⊆ A, so κ_j({f = t}) = κ_j({f = t} ∩ A) = (κ_j⌞A)({f = t}) = 0.
9. D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t). Put u_j(h) := ofReal(h⁻¹)·ν_j({t − h < f < t}). The sequence h_k tends to 0 through positive values, i.e. along atTop it tends to 0 within (0, ∞); a liminf along the finer filter (the image of atTop under k ↦ h_k) is at least the liminf along 𝓝[>] 0, so D_j(t) ≤ liminf_k u_j(h_k). For all k with h_k < t − a (all large k, since h_k → 0 < t − a): a < t − h_k and t < b give {t − h_k < f < t} ⊆ A, so ν_j({t − h_k < f < t}) = ν_j(f⁻¹((t − h_k, t)) ∩ A) = ρ_j((t − h_k, t)); and ofReal(h_k⁻¹) = k + 1. Hence u_j(h_k) = F_{j,k}(t) for all large k, and liminf_k u_j(h_k) = G_j(t). Therefore D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t).
10. (ii). D_j(t) ≤ G_j(t) < ∞ by steps 7 and 9.
11. (iii). liminf_j G_j(t) = H(t) = 0, so for every n ∈ ℕ there are infinitely many j with G_j(t) < 1/(n + 1). Choose φ(0) < φ(1) < ⋯ inductively with G_{φ(n)}(t) < 1/(n + 1) (Mathlib extraction_forall_of_frequently). Then 0 ≤ D_{φ(n)}(t) ≤ G_{φ(n)}(t) < 1/(n + 1) → 0. ∎

  intro P ν κ f a b hf hab hνfin hνlim hκfin
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ : ∃ A : Set (Euclid P), A = {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b} := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hA] at hνfin hνlim hκfin
  have hAm : MeasurableSet A := by
    rw [hA]
    exact (measurableSet_lt measurable_const hf).inter (measurableSet_lt hf measurable_const)
  -- Step 1: push the restricted measures forward to the line
  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ⟩ : ∃ ρ : ℕ → Measure ℝ, ρ = fun j => ((ν j).restrict A).map f := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have hρapp : ∀ j (s : Set ℝ), MeasurableSet s → ρ j s = ν j (f ⁻¹' s ∩ A) := by
    intro j s hs
    rw [hρ, Measure.map_apply hf hs, Measure.restrict_apply (hf hs)]
  have hρuniv : ∀ j, ρ j univ = ν j A := by
    intro j
    rw [hρapp j univ MeasurableSet.univ, preimage_univ, univ_inter]
  have hρfin : ∀ j, IsFiniteMeasure (ρ j) := fun j => ⟨by rw [hρuniv]; exact hνfin j⟩
  -- Step 2: Tonelli for the strips
  have hSm : ∀ c : ℝ, MeasurableSet {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 - c < p.2 ∧ p.2 < p.1} := fun c =>
    (measurableSet_lt (measurable_fst.sub_const c) measurable_snd).inter
      (measurableSet_lt measurable_snd measurable_fst)
  have hsec : ∀ c t : ℝ, Prod.mk t ⁻¹' {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 - c < p.2 ∧ p.2 < p.1} = Ioo (t - c) t := by
    intro c t
    ext y
    simp [mem_Ioo]
  have hsec' : ∀ c y : ℝ,
      (fun t => (t, y)) ⁻¹' {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.1 - c < p.2 ∧ p.2 < p.1} = Ioo y (y + c) := by
    intro c y
    ext t
    simp only [mem_preimage, mem_ofPred_eq, mem_Ioo]
    constructor <;> rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ <;> constructor <;> linarith

    intro j c

    intro j c

    simp only [hsec, hsec', Real.volume_Ioo, add_sub_cancel_left] at h1 h2

    intro k
    have hk : ENNReal.ofReal ((k : ℝ) + 1) = (k : ℝ≥0∞) + 1 := by

      ∫⁻ t, ((k : ℝ≥0∞) + 1) * ρ j (Ioo (t - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) t) = ν j A := by

    ae_all_iff.2 fun j => ae_lt_top (hDm j) ((hDint j).trans_lt (hνfin j)).ne

    rw [ae_all_iff]
    intro j
    have : IsFiniteMeasure ((κ j).restrict A) :=

    have hc := Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos (μ := (κ j).restrict A) hf

    rw [Real.volume_Ioo]
    simpa using hab

  obtain ⟨t, ht, hHt, hDt, hκt⟩ := hgood.exists

    show liminf ((fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * ν j {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t}) ∘
      fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) atTop = _

Both pass an inequality between Radon measures from open neighbourhoods of a compact set to the set itself by continuity from above; this child states that step once, for the neighbourhoods E_δ.

1. If E = ∅ then μ(E) = 0 and there is nothing to prove; the argument below also covers this case. Choose δ > 0 with C_δ := {x : dist(x, E) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := δ/(k + 2) ∈ (0, δ) and G_k := {x : dist(x, E) < r_k} (open thickening).

Since r_k decreases, (G_k) is decreasing. ⋂_k G_k = E: E ⊆ G_k for all k; conversely, if dist(x, E) < r_k for all k, then for every ε > 0 some r_k < ε gives x ∈ {dist(·, E) < ε}, so x ∈ ⋂_{ε>0} {dist(·, E) < ε} = closure(E) (Metric.closure_eq_iInter_thickening) = E, E being compact and hence closed.
